mice 3.20.0

Source: news_3.20.0.md

Major changes

  • Parallel imputation inside mice(). With mice(..., future = TRUE), each of the m chains of the Gibbs sampler runs over all iterations as a separate future on the plan set by the user, e.g. plan(multisession), plan(future.mirai::mirai_multisession) or a cluster. mice() never sets or changes the plan. The results are combined into one mids object, including chainMean, chainVar and loggedEvents. Each chain gets its own random number stream, so results are reproducible with seed and do not depend on the number of workers, but they differ from future = FALSE. The default future = FALSE is the classic sequential sampler and is unchanged. User-defined imputation methods (e.g. mice.impute.mymethod() in the global environment) and the global objects used in post are sent to the workers. With print = TRUE, mice() reports the plan and the number of workers. The mids object has two new fields: future (a list with plan, workers and pid) and chainSeed (the state of the random number stream of each chain). mice.mids() gains the argument future. By default, an object created with future = TRUE continues as futures, with the same result as one mice() call with all iterations. rbind(), cbind(), filter() and ibind() keep the new fields. Thanks 1 for advice (#735, #736). Requires future and future.apply. See the vignettes Parallel imputation and Parallel imputation: benchmarks.

  • Progress reporting through the progressr package. mice() and mice.mids() signal one step after each iteration of each chain (m * maxit steps), both sequentially and with future = TRUE. Enable it with progressr::with_progress(mice(...)) or progressr::handlers(global = TRUE). Nothing is shown without a handler, and the imputations do not change. Based on the idea in #750 by Joshua Carpenter (see also #516, #551, #565).

  • D3() now follows Meng and Rubin (1992) exactly. The deviance of the constrained models is evaluated with all parameters fixed at their pooled values, including the nuisance parameters: the residual variance in lm and gaussian glm, and the variance components in lmer models. Models fitted by REML are refitted by ML. For these classes D3() gives the same result as mitml::testModels(method = "D3"). Previously, D3() re-estimated the nuisance parameters, which inflated the statistic somewhat. For other model classes D3() keeps the previous approach. D3() now warns when the statistic is negative, e.g. under separation in logistic regression.

  • Adds mice.impute.svm() for imputing binary variables in high-dimensional data by Support Vector Machines combined with bootstrapping (#751, #752). Contributed @mtakahashi123

  • Adds the random.effects argument to mice.impute.2l.bin() with options "laplace" (default), "eb" and "marginal", implementing the FCS-GLM distinction between sporadic and systematic missingness of Audigier et al. (2018). Also vectorises the imputation loop (#686). The new vignette random-effects-2l-bin discusses the three strategies.

  • Fewer hard dependencies. glmnet and mitml move from Imports to Suggests. They are only needed by the lasso methods, D1(), D2(), mice.impute.panImpute() and mice.impute.jomoImpute(), which ask to install them on demand. This removes about 30 packages from the installation of mice, including foreach, jomo, pan, lme4, haven and readr. Requires R 4.1.0 or later, which broom, dplyr and tidyr already required. Removes the unused cpp11 entry from LinkingTo.

Breaking changes

  • PMM results change for tied predicted values. Fixes miscalibrated donor selection in matchindex(), the default PMM matching engine since mice 3.11.8, when many target cases share the same (or nearly the same) predicted value, e.g. intercept-only models, models with few categorical predictors, or heavily rounded outcomes. Ties were broken once per imputed dataset, so all tied target cases drew from the same small set of donors. This inflated the between-imputation variance and gave too wide confidence intervals. Ties are now broken independently for each target case. Affected versions: mice 3.11.8 through 3.19.11. To reproduce earlier results, install that version, e.g. remotes::install_version("mice", version = "3.19.0") (#757, #236).

  • The confidence interval columns of summary(pool(fit), conf.int = TRUE), summary.mipo() and pool.table() are named conf.low and conf.high (broom convention) instead of 2.5 % and 97.5 %. Duplicate CI columns in summary.mipo() are removed (#719).

  • The D3 statistics and p-values for lm, gaussian glm and lmer models change (see above).

  • mice.mids() with newdata now inherits the imputation methods from the mids object instead of re-initializing them, so that training and deployment imputation models behave the same (#753). A variable that had no missing values in the training data has method "". If newdata has missing values in such a variable, mice.mids() assigns the default method for its type and says so in a message. Without this, the missing values stayed NA, and could also leave other variables NA when used as a predictor. A method "" that the user set is kept. See the vignette Imputing new data.

  • Fixes an error “Length of method differs from number of blocks” in mice.mids() with newdata when the model was trained with formulas or blocks that do not cover all variables.

  • The internal logging object is renamed from state to .mice.state (#527). Extension packages whose mice.impute.* functions call mice:::updateLog() outside the Gibbs sampler of mice() will no longer find the logging state.

  • The mipo class no longer inherits from data.frame. The new as.data.frame.mipo() returns summary(), which repairs knitr::kable() and rmarkdown::paged_table() on mipo objects (#733).

Minor changes

  • mice() and mice.mids() gain the argument print, which replaces printFlag as the recommended way to silence the iteration history, e.g. mice(nhanes, print = FALSE). Set the default with options(mice.print = FALSE). printFlag and options(mice.printFlag) keep working; if both print and printFlag are given, printFlag takes precedence.
  • Errors in an imputation method or a post statement now report where the sampler stopped, e.g. mice() stopped at iteration 3, imputation 2, variable 'bmi' (method 'pmm'), followed by the original message. The error has class mice_sampler_error with fields iteration, imputation, variable, method, post and parent.
  • post expressions can use the new variable chain, the imputation number, e.g. imp[[j]][, i] <- imp[[j]][, i] + delta[chain].
  • method = "rf" caps the number of threads of ranger and literanger at parallelly::availableCores(), so that futures do not compete for cores and scheduler limits (Slurm, containers) are respected. A thread count set by the user takes precedence. num.threads and n_thread are now also used for prediction. The imputations do not change.
  • futuremice() determines the number of cores by parallelly::availableCores(omit = 1, max = m), which works on a single-core machine, and restores the future plan that was active before the call instead of resetting it to sequential (#735). Thanks
    1. Requires parallelly 1.45.0 or later.
  • parlmice() no longer changes the RNG kind of the session to L'Ecuyer-CMRG.
  • mice() warns when the data contain POSIXct or POSIXlt columns, which can make the predictor matrix near-singular, and estimice() gives an informative error when the ridge-penalised solve() fails (#746).
  • Reformats the R source with the Air formatter (#721).
  • Cleans up the testthat suite, and gives every test_that() label a stable <FUNCTION>-<NNN> ID (e.g. BARNARD-RUBIN-001) for comparison with other implementations. Tests that compare separate mice() runs use expect_equal(), as MKL is not bitwise reproducible.
  • Fixes math rendering in the documentation and the link to the mcar() reference (#769). Thanks @saikrishna488
  • Updates bibliography entries.

Bug fixes

  • Fixes a bug where an argument in ... that partially matched an argument of the internal sampler shifted the positional arguments, so that the value of printFlag reached the imputation methods. This silently changed imputations, e.g. rf used one tree instead of ntree, in particular with futuremice(..., print = FALSE).
  • Fixes pool() returning dfcom = 1 for clmm models from ordinal, which gave wrong degrees of freedom, p-values and confidence intervals (#748).
  • Fixes barnard.rubin() returning only the first element for vector b and dfcom = Inf.
  • Fixes “invalid factor level” warnings in mice.impute.midastouch() for factors with non-default levels (#738).
  • Fixes dim(X) must have a positive length in mice.impute.polr(), mice.impute.lda() and mice.impute.polyreg() with one missing value (#684).
  • Fixes $ operator is invalid for atomic vectors when the data or the global environment contains a variable named state (#527).
  • Fixes a crash in the chain statistics when the data contain character variables (#601).
  • Preserves logical variables in complete() (#764, #765). Thanks @dajiaohuang
  • Fixes a bug in mcar() (#762, #763).
  • Fixes ampute(run = FALSE) (#732).
